name: Explain how diction, register or tone creates a stated effect
definition: [Tier 2 derived, unvalidated] Name the register, tone or word-level choice the question asks about and explain the effect it creates on the reader or the message, instead of only labelling it. name: Identify and correct an error of grammar, concord or spelling in context
definition: [Tier 2 derived, unvalidated] Locate the specific error in the supplied sentence and supply its corrected form; the task is error repair, not general rewriting. name: Explain how sentence construction or punctuation shapes meaning
definition: [Tier 2 derived, unvalidated] Name the syntactic or punctuation feature (repetition and commas, voice, hyphen, capitals, sentence type) and explain what it does to the meaning, emphasis or reader of the sentence. name: Interpret a poem's imagery, connotation or tone and its effect
definition: [Tier 2 derived, unvalidated] Identify the figure, image or connotative word the question targets and explain the effect it creates in the poem; naming the device without its work does not answer the question. [sources: english_2016_internal_paper1_nov_q4.2, english_2016_internal_paper1_nov_q4.3, english_2017_internal_paper1_nov_q3.1, english_2017_internal_paper1_nov_q3.3, english_2017_internal_paper1_nov_q3.7.2, english_2018_internal_paper1_july_q4.2, english_2018_internal_paper1_july_q4.3]

name: Explain how a poem's structure, form or punctuation shapes its meaning
definition: [Tier 2 derived, unvalidated] Explain what line arrangement, enjambment, repetition or punctuation does to the pace, emphasis or meaning of the poem, rather than describing the stanza. [sources: english_2016_internal_paper1_nov_q4.4, english_2017_internal_paper1_nov_q3.4, english_2017_internal_paper1_nov_q3.5, english_2018_internal_paper1_july_q3.1, english_2018_internal_paper1_july_q3.2, english_2018_internal_paper1_july_q3.3]

subject: english

name: Explain a character's motive, change or responsibility using the whole set work
definition: [Tier 2 derived, unvalidated] Account for what a named character does, feels or becomes, and support it with evidence from outside the printed extract; describing the plot does not answer the question. [sources: english_2014_internal_paper2_july_q1.4, english_2014_internal_paper2_july_q1.6, english_2014_internal_paper2_july_q1.7, english_2015_internal_paper2_july_q1.2, english_2015_internal_paper2_july_q1.6, english_2015_internal_paper2_july_q1.7, english_2015_internal_paper2_july_q1.8]

name: Recall and relate a specific event, relationship or reference from the set work
definition: [Tier 2 derived, unvalidated] State the particular event, relationship or term the question asks about, in the terms the text itself uses; it is a recall task, not a judgment task. [sources: english_2014_internal_paper2_july_q1.1, english_2014_internal_paper2_july_q1.2, english_2014_internal_paper2_july_q1.5, english_2014_internal_paper2_july_q1.8, english_2015_internal_paper2_july_q1.1, english_2015_internal_paper2_july_q1.3]
subject: english

name: Interpret an image, statement or relationship in a set-work extract
definition: [Tier 2 derived, unvalidated] Turn a quoted image, statement or relationship in the printed extract into its meaning in the text, quoting the extract as the memo requires. [sources: english_2014_internal_paper2_july_q1.3, english_2014_internal_paper2_july_q1.9, english_2015_internal_paper2_july_q1.4, english_2015_internal_paper2_july_q1.5]

name: Construct a dictionary entry for a word or neologism in context
definition: [Tier 2 derived, unvalidated] Give the requested components of a dictionary entry (part of speech, definition, and where asked etymology) for the coinage or word as it is used in the supplied text. [sources: english_2017_internal_paper1_nov_q5.3, english_2018_internal_paper1_july_q1.7.2]
subject: english

name: Evaluate the reliability, positioning or success of an argument
definition: [Tier 2 derived, unvalidated] Take a position on how reliable, successfully positioned or effective the writer's argument is and substantiate it with the text's own evidence, rather than summarising the argument. [sources: english_2016_internal_paper1_nov_q1.9, english_2017_internal_paper1_nov_q1.10, english_2018_internal_paper1_july_q1.5, english_2018_internal_paper1_july_q1.8]
subject: english

name: Explain the meaning and effect of an idiom or fixed expression
definition: [Tier 2 derived, unvalidated] Unpack what the idiom or altered expression means in its paragraph and, where asked, the effect of its use or the difference from the standard form. [sources: english_2016_internal_paper1_nov_q1.2, english_2016_internal_paper1_nov_q1.6, english_2017_internal_paper1_nov_q1.7, english_2018_internal_paper1_july_q1.3]
subject: english

name: Draw out the implication of a metaphor or extended comparison
definition: [Tier 2 derived, unvalidated] Interpret the comparison the writer reaches for (a metaphor, a cartoon figure, a metaphor built from a natural object) and what it implies about the subject. [sources: english_2016_internal_paper1_nov_q1.4, english_2017_internal_paper1_nov_q1.4, english_2018_internal_paper1_july_q1.2]
subject: english

name: Explain the stated idea, message or title of a poem with quotation
definition: [Tier 2 derived, unvalidated] Explain the poem's central message, title or a stated idea and support the reading with quotation from the poem, as the memo demands. [sources: english_2016_internal_paper1_nov_q3.1, english_2016_internal_paper1_nov_q3.2, english_2016_internal_paper1_nov_q3.4, english_2016_internal_paper1_nov_q4.1, english_2017_internal_paper1_nov_q3.2, english_2017_internal_paper1_nov_q3.6, english_2017_internal_paper1_nov_q3.9, english_2018_internal_paper1_july_q3.4, english_2018_internal_paper1_july_q4.1]

name: Explain the effect of a rhetorical or opening device
definition: [Tier 2 derived, unvalidated] Judge or explain what the opening move or rhetorical question does for the reader and the writer's purpose, tying it to the text's intention. [sources: english_2016_internal_paper1_nov_q1.1, english_2017_internal_paper1_nov_q1.1, english_2018_internal_paper1_july_q1.6]
